sources.title: Causality and the Semantics of Provenance
sources.date_basis: arXiv initial submission 2010-04-19; later published in EPTCS.
overlap: Separates provenance notions such as influence and dependence from formal causality and argues that causal semantics must be established separately.
non_overlap: Does not provide an AI-agent mutation benchmark or a cross-layer governance taxonomy.

sources.title: StateBench — conformance test for stateful AI systems
overlap: Defines an executable multi-class failure taxonomy for stateful agents including resurrection, stale reasoning, authority violation, scope leak and temporal decay.
Uses conformance tests and corrected scoring rather than prose-only warnings.
non_overlap: Does not model receipt/evidence promotions such as approval-to-execution, invocation-to-effect or provenance-to-causality under one typed oracle.

sources.title: Causality Laundering: Denial-Feedback Leakage in Tool-Calling LLM Agents
overlap: Names and evaluates a failure where causal influence of a denied action escapes through a later benign action and flat provenance is insufficient.
Provides controlled attack scenarios and a runtime causal-provenance monitor.
non_overlap: Focuses on denial-feedback causal leakage rather than a general taxonomy across epistemic, authority, review and execution transitions.

sources.title: Quantifying Potential Observation Missingness in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
overlap: Distinguishes recorded observations from information that may have been available to the original decision-maker and measures consequences of missing decision-time observations.
non_overlap: Does not define a named availability-to-intent failure or authority/action receipt benchmark.

sources.title: Anchored Parallax Log — decontextualization, frame laundering and semantic overclaim
sources.date_basis: Public motivation page records last update 2026-05-14; current protocol identifies the project as April 2026, so 2026-05-14 is used as a conservative no-later-than public bound.
overlap: Explicitly names semantic overclaim: extrapolating a narrow benchmark observation into overall quality, safety or readiness.
Uses content-addressed frames, declared exclusions, explicit bridges and deterministic validation to prevent silent semantic drift.
non_overlap: Primarily governs interpretation of frame-bound observations rather than authorization, human review or execution effects.

sources.title: AIRGuard: Guarding Agent Actions with Runtime Authority Control
overlap: Names authority confusion: untrusted resources may inform reasoning but must not authorize side effects.
Evaluates a runtime authority-control defense on AgentTrap and DTAP-150 with ablations.
non_overlap: Does not attempt one taxonomy spanning semantic overclaim, state resurrection, provenance/causality and execution-evidence inflation.

sources.title: Provenance-Bound Context Attestation and Deterministic Policy Authorization for Agentic AI Actions
sources.date_basis: Zenodo record created 2026-06-04; later SSRN posting is not used as the earliest bound.
overlap: Treats self-declared orchestration context as insufficient for authorization and inserts provenance-bound context attestation before deterministic policy evaluation.
Uses a structured 170-scenario benchmark plus a 12-scenario robustness probe.
non_overlap: Targets context provenance at the authorization boundary rather than a general heterogeneous semantic-promotion taxonomy.

sources.title: An Agent Action Capsule Profile for SCITT
overlap: Separates authorization records from what an agent actually did and represents action/outcome evidence with typed dispositions.
non_overlap: Does not define a broad named fault taxonomy across state, epistemics, causality and authority.

sources.title: Authorization Evidence Chains: Composing Heterogeneous Agent-Authorization Receipts
overlap: Treats identity, delegation, permit, human authorization and transparency receipts as complementary evidence classes with their own verification rules rather than interchangeable authority.
non_overlap: Its composition target is authorization evidence for one action, not a general semantic escalation benchmark across truth, memory, causality and execution.

sources.title: A SCITT Profile for AI-Agent Action Receipts
overlap: Defines narrow per-action receipts and explicitly limits what authenticity of action/principal/policy/verdict proves about safety, inputs and real-world outcome.
non_overlap: Does not expose one cross-layer mutation corpus spanning non-execution semantic classes.

sources.title: The Witnessed Execution Protocol (WEXP): Core Specification
overlap: Defines one verifier discipline over distinct content bases observation, intent, invocation and execution; the structural order is explicitly not entailment and each base must be evaluated independently.
Normatively forbids intent->authority/execution, invocation->execution/effect, provenance->runtime occurrence, signature->truth and transparency receipt->execution inferences.
Includes deterministic appraisal verdicts and conformance vectors.
non_overlap: Its axis is execution-evidence strength; it does not include resource availability/consideration, responsibility acceptance, coordination or human-AI authorship governance as peer semantic bases.

sources.title: QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement: Separating Receipt from Authorization for Downstream Effect
overlap: Explicitly separates technical receipt from authority for downstream effect and requires separate evidence, policy, freshness and origin checks.
non_overlap: Specialized receipt/effect boundary rather than a cross-domain semantic escalation taxonomy.

sources.title: AI Agent Approval vs. Authorization: Why the Difference Matters
sources.date_basis: Page reviewed date 2026-08-22; same calendar day as the public UU-AAP repository anchor, so it is conservatively treated as parallel rather than predecessor evidence.
overlap: States that human approval is evidence, not the whole authorization decision; current identity, policy, payload, reviewer and expiry must still be checked before dispatch.
non_overlap: Practitioner guidance, not a cross-layer benchmark or standards specification.

sources.title: Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering / EAL-Bench
sources.date_basis: arXiv initial submission 2026-09-01, after the 2026-08-22 public UU-AAP anchor.
overlap: Formalizes false authority created in persistent memory and measures propagation to unauthorized tool actions with a hidden deterministic authorization ledger across three domains.
non_overlap: Postdates the UU-AAP public anchor and therefore is convergence evidence only; it cannot defeat a pre-existing August 2026 claim in this audit.
